title: Full Frontal
verdict_short: No. Just Brad Pitt being Brad Pitt on a film set.
how: Pitt appears as himself in Soderbergh's meta Hollywood comedy, showing up on the set of the movie-within-the-movie where actor Nicholas (Blair Underwood) is pulled away to shoot a scene alongside him. His only stake in the story is being reassured that his movie is 'the real movie.' He is never in any peril and simply exits the story as the day-in-the-life plot moves on.
notes: Celebrity cameo as himself; not a character with a fate.

title: Confessions of a Dangerous Mind
verdict_short: No. He just loses on The Dating Game.
how: In George Clooney's directorial debut, Pitt and Matt Damon sit on stools in period wigs and loud 1970s outfits as two contestants on Chuck Barris's The Dating Game. The bachelorette ignores them entirely, and neither gets a line; the joke restages the real-life fact that Burt Reynolds and Tom Selleck went unpicked on the show. Pitt's screen time is a few seconds, and he simply isn't chosen.
notes: Blink-and-miss-it cameo done as a favor to Clooney. No peril of any kind.

title: Jackass
verdict_short: No. Kidnapped at Pink's Hot Dogs, but it's a prank.
how: Pitt turned up in two Season 3 episodes of MTV's Jackass in 2002. In 'Night Monkey 2' he dons a gorilla suit with Johnny Knoxville, Bam Margera, Chris Pontius and Steve-O and rampages through the streets of Los Angeles. In 'The Abduction' he stands in line at Pink's Hot Dogs in Hollywood when masked men grab him, drag him thrashing into a van and drive off while horrified bystanders try to intervene. It's all staged; he walks away unharmed.
notes: Reality/prank TV, no fictional character. Pitt does not appear in Jackass Number Two (2006) despite frequent misattribution.

title: Sinbad: Legend of the Seven Seas
verdict_short: No. The executioner's sword shatters mid-swing.
how: Framed by the goddess Eris for stealing the Book of Peace, Sinbad is sentenced to death, but Prince Proteus takes his place as hostage while Sinbad sails to Tartarus to recover it. Eris offers Sinbad a bargain: if he answers truthfully whether he'll return to face execution, she'll surrender the Book. He returns to Syracuse and kneels for the blade, but because he answered honestly, an enraged Eris must honor the deal, shattering the executioner's sword and delivering the Book. Sinbad is pardoned and sails off with Marina, who stows away on his ship.
notes: Comes within a sword-swing of a beheading in the climax but is saved by divine contract. Animated voice role.

title: Abby Singer
verdict_short: No. Tells a struggling actor he's done at an awards show.
how: Micro-budget indie shot guerrilla-style; Pitt appears backstage as himself.
notes: Uncredited, documentary-style cameo.

title: King of the Hill
verdict_short: No. Dumped at the altar for being a sleaze.
how: Boomhauer's womanizing brother Patch rolls into Arlen in a Saab convertible to marry Katherine (Laura Dern), Boomhauer's old flame. Boomhauer quits as best man and Hank steps in, assuming Boomhauer is sabotaging the wedding, until it becomes clear Patch is the one sneaking around. When Patch blurts out the truth, Katherine hands back the ring and calls off the engagement. Patch is left humiliated but alive.
notes: Season 8 premiere, aired November 2, 2003. Pitt, a fan of the show, pitched the idea of voicing Boomhauer's brother; the character speaks in the same Boomhauer mumble.

title: Troy
verdict_short: Yes. Paris's arrow finds the famous heel.
how: During the sack of Troy, Achilles ignores the slaughter and searches the burning city for Briseis. He finds her just as Paris, seeking vengeance for Hector, puts an arrow through his heel and then several more into his chest. Achilles pulls the body-shots out so that only the heel wound is seen, watches Briseis flee with Paris, and dies on the temple steps. Odysseus cremates him in the closing funeral scene and narrates his legend.
notes: Follows the myth's heel wound, though the film has Paris finish him with multiple arrows to the torso; Achilles yanks those out so the legend of the single heel shot can stand.

title: Ocean's Twelve
verdict_short: No. Out-cons the Night Fox and gets the girl.
how: Rusty is Danny Ocean's right hand as the crew scrambles across Europe to repay Terry Benedict, competing with the Night Fox to steal the Fabergé Coronation Egg. His ex, Europol detective Isabel Lahiri, lifts his phone and arrests most of the gang, but it turns out the real egg was swiped by Linus's parents and mentor Gaspar LeMarc days earlier. Rusty ends the film taking Isabel to a safe house where she meets her father, LeMarc, and the crew walks free.
notes: Nobody in the crew is ever in mortal danger; the stakes are financial and legal.

title: Mr. & Mrs. Smith
verdict_short: No. Survives his wife and a store full of assassins.
how: Rival contract killers John and Jane Smith discover they've been married to the enemy and set about killing each other, leveling their suburban house in a shootout. With guns drawn they realize they can't pull the trigger, reconcile, and learn their agencies have ordered both of them dead. They make a last stand in a home-improvement store, mowing down waves of hitmen, and the film ends with the couple back in marriage counseling, beaming about how well things are going.
notes: John takes plenty of punishment from Jane but nothing fatal.

title: Babel
verdict_short: No. His wife takes the bullet, and she lives too.
how: Richard and Susan are American tourists in Morocco, their marriage strained by the recent crib death of their infant son, when a stray rifle shot fired by two goat-herder boys hits Susan through the tour-bus window. Richard drags her to a remote village, where a local vet stitches the wound and the other tourists abandon them. After an agonizing wait, a helicopter finally airlifts them to a hospital in Casablanca, where Susan is expected to recover. Richard is never physically harmed.
notes: The wounded character is Cate Blanchett's Susan, not Pitt's Richard; she survives.

title: Ocean's Thirteen
verdict_short: No. Walks off grinning after a rigged $11 million slot win.
how: Rusty helps Danny orchestrate revenge on casino mogul Willy Bank, who cheated their friend Reuben into a heart attack. The crew rigs every game on The Bank's opening night, fakes an earthquake with a tunnel-boring drill, and empties the casino. In the final scene at the airport, Rusty gives his last coin to the real Five Diamond reviewer, who wins $11 million on a rigged slot machine as Rusty strolls away smiling.
notes: Third and final Rusty appearance; no physical danger at any point.

title: The Assassination of Jesse James by the Coward Robert Ford
verdict_short: Yes. Shot in the back of the head by Robert Ford.
how: On the morning of April 3, 1882, in his St. Joseph, Missouri home, Jesse reads a newspaper report of Dick Liddil's surrender and realizes the Fords have betrayed him. Seemingly resigned, he removes his gun belt, climbs onto a chair and turns his back to dust a framed picture on the wall. Robert Ford draws the nickel-plated revolver Jesse had gifted him days earlier and shoots him in the back of the head. Jesse crumples to the floor, dead, and the Fords flee to claim the reward.
notes: The film strongly implies Jesse knows what's coming and allows it. The death occurs roughly two hours in, followed by a long epilogue tracing Ford's own downfall and murder.

title: Burn After Reading
verdict_short: Yes. Shot in the face in a closet by Harry Pfarrer.
how: Dim, exuberant gym trainer Chad breaks into Osborne Cox's house to dig up more 'intelligence' and hides in a bedroom closet when Harry Pfarrer (George Clooney), a jumpy U.S. Marshal sleeping with Cox's wife, comes home. Harry opens the closet door, Chad grins nervously, and Harry reflexively shoots him in the head. Finding no ID and the tags cut from Chad's suit, Harry concludes he's killed a government spy and dumps the body. The CIA later finds the corpse and quietly buries the whole affair.
notes: Abrupt, played for shock comedy; Chad's death comes roughly two-thirds through and derails every character's scheme.

title: The Curious Case of Benjamin Button
verdict_short: Yes. Dies of old age as a newborn in Daisy's arms.
how: Born in 1918 with the body of an old man and aging backward, Benjamin spends his last years regressing into childhood. In 1990 Daisy finds him as a pre-teen with dementia and takes him into the nursing home where he was raised; he shrinks into a toddler, then an infant, his mind fading. In spring 2003, chronologically 85 but physically a newborn, he looks up at Daisy, seems to recognize her, closes his eyes and dies in her arms. Daisy recounts all this from her own deathbed in 2005 as Hurricane Katrina approaches.
notes: The whole film is narrated from Benjamin's diary by a dying Daisy, so his death is both shown and framed as memory.

title: Inglourious Basterds
verdict_short: No. Carves his masterpiece into Landa's forehead.
how: Aldo 'the Apache' Raine leads the Basterds' Nazi-scalping campaign through occupied France and gets captured by Col. Hans Landa at the Paris premiere after a bungled Italian cover. Landa cuts a deal with the Allies to let Operation Kino proceed, and Hitler, Goebbels and the Nazi high command burn and are shot to pieces inside the cinema. Driving Raine and Utivich to American lines, Landa surrenders; Raine shoots Landa's radio operator and, deciding a deal shouldn't let Landa take off his uniform, carves a swastika into his forehead with his knife.
notes: Raine is captured and beaten but never seriously hurt. Donowitz and Ulmer die in the cinema blast; Raine and Utivich are the survivors.

title: Beyond All Boundaries
verdict_short: No.
how: Museum documentary narration.

title: Megamind
verdict_short: No. Fakes his death to become Music Man.
how: Early on, Megamind lures Metro Man to the old observatory and blasts him with a sun-powered death ray, apparently vaporizing him; the hero had claimed the copper-lined dome weakened his powers, and only a charred cape and skeleton are left. Metro City mourns and Megamind takes over, then grows bored without a nemesis. Midway through, Megamind and Roxanne discover Metro Man alive in his secret hideout, where he confesses he faked the copper weakness and his own death because he was burned out on heroing and wants to play guitar. He returns in disguise at the end to cheer Megamind's turn as the city's hero.
notes: Fake death: staged by death ray in the first act, revealed as a hoax at the midpoint. Metro Man is alive and well at the end.

title: The Tree of Life
verdict_short: No. It's his son who dies; he outlives the boy.
how: The film opens with Mr. and Mrs. O'Brien receiving the telegram that their 19-year-old son R.L. has died in the 1960s, and the rest unfolds as older son Jack's memories of a 1950s Texas childhood under his stern, frustrated father. Mr. O'Brien, an engineer and thwarted musician, loses a patent suit and his plant closes, and in a moment of humility asks Jack's forgiveness before the family moves away. He is last seen alive, and in the film's beach-of-eternity coda the whole family, R.L. included, is reunited.
notes: The film's central death is R.L.'s, delivered by telegram in the opening minutes. The afterlife/beach sequence is metaphysical, not a literal death of Mr. O'Brien.

title: Moneyball
verdict_short: No. Turns down $12.5 million and stays in Oakland.
how: Oakland A's general manager Billy Beane rebuilds a gutted roster on sabermetrics with Yale economist Peter Brand, endures a brutal start, and rides a record 20-game winning streak capped by Scott Hatteberg's walk-off homer. The A's win the AL West but lose the divisional series to Minnesota. The Red Sox offer Beane the richest GM contract in sports history; he declines it to stay near his daughter, listening to her song in his car as the film closes.
notes: Biographical; the real Billy Beane is alive. No physical peril in the film beyond thrown chairs.

title: Happy Feet Two
verdict_short: No. A krill who refuses to be eaten and becomes a legend.
how: Will, an existentially restless krill, drags his friend Bill (Matt Damon) away from the swarm to climb the food chain, only to learn he's at the very bottom of it. After a series of near-misses with whales and predators, a humbled Will reunites with Bill and the swarm, where they're hailed as legends for their journey. In the finale Will and the krill join the penguins, elephant seals and Sven in the mass effort to shatter the iceberg trapping the emperor penguins.
notes: Comic side plot; despite being prey, neither krill is eaten. Animated voice role.

title: Killing Them Softly
verdict_short: No. America's not a country, it's a business. Now pay him.
how: Mob enforcer Jackie Cogan is brought in to clean up after a protected card game is robbed, and he does: he has Markie Trattman gunned down in his car, blasts Squirrel with a shotgun at a meet, and shoots Frankie in the head without warning in a parking garage. Nobody ever gets a shot at Jackie himself. On election night 2008 he meets the mob's lawyer Driver in a bar, is offered a discounted fee, and delivers the closing monologue before demanding his full money.
notes: Jackie is the film's only unscathed principal; Mickey (Gandolfini) is arrested and everyone else is killed.

title: World War Z
verdict_short: No. Injects himself with a deadly pathogen and walks right past the zombies.
how: Ex-UN investigator Gerry Lane survives the Philadelphia outbreak, a rooftop extraction in Newark, the fall of Jerusalem, and a plane crash outside Cardiff that leaves him impaled by shrapnel. At the WHO lab he theorizes that the undead ignore the terminally ill, so with a zombie blocking the vault door he injects himself with a lethal but curable pathogen, walks untouched through the infected wing, and is cured. He reaches his family at a Nova Scotia safe zone as a 'camouflage' vaccine turns the tide.
notes: Comes close several times. The famously reshot third act replaced a bleaker Moscow ending in which Gerry also survived.

title: 12 Years a Slave
verdict_short: No. The Canadian carpenter who mails the letter that frees Solomon.
how: Late in the film, Canadian itinerant laborer Samuel Bass arrives at Edwin Epps's plantation to build a gazebo alongside Solomon Northup and openly argues with Epps that slavery is an abomination. After Solomon confides that he is a kidnapped free man, Bass risks his life to write to Solomon's friends in Saratoga, New York. The letter brings the sheriff and shopkeeper Mr. Parker to the plantation, and Solomon is freed after twelve years. Bass simply finishes his work and departs unharmed.
notes: Small but pivotal role near the end of the film; Pitt also produced through Plan B.

title: The Counselor
verdict_short: Yes. Decapitated on a London street by the bolito.
how: Middleman Westray, who earlier warned the Counselor about the cartel's 'bolito', a motorized wire loop that tightens until it cuts through the neck, flees to London with his money when the drug deal goes bad. Malkina hires a woman to seduce him and steal his bank codes, then has her men snatch his laptop and drop the bolito over his head on a crowded sidewalk. The device whirs tighter as Westray claws at it and collapses in a spreading pool of blood, and the wire finally severs his head. Malkina drains his accounts and escapes.
notes: One of the most infamous death scenes of the 2010s; the device is foreshadowed in Westray's own earlier monologue.
